'''Claire Berger''' is a French physicist at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] and a Director of Research at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS). Berger has co-authored over 200 publications in international journals and has a citation index of 10,880. She has won a number of prizes including the CNRS medal for Young Researcher and the {{ill|Louis Ancel Prize (physics)|lt=Louis Ancel Prize|fr|Prix Louis-Ancel}} of the [[French Physical Society]]. She was elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="Physics">{{cite web|url=https://www.physics.gatech.edu/user/claire-berger|title=Claire Berger : Research Scientist|publisher=Physics.gatech.edu|accessdate=28 December 2014}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Claire Berger was born in Paris.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-09-20 |title=Claire Berger Receives one of France’s Highest Civilian Honors in Science, Scientific Diplomacy |url=https://physics.gatech.edu/news/claire-berger-receives-one-frances-highest-civilian-honors-science-scientific-diplomacy |access-date=2026-08-10 |website=School of Physics |language=en}}</ref>

Berger took as the subject of her PhD the electronic properties of AIMn quasicrystals. She gained her doctorate at the [[Joseph Fourier University]], now part of the [[University of Grenoble]], France,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=C. Berger |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37395161200 |access-date=2026-08-10 |website=ieeexplore.ieee.org}}</ref> making hers the first thesis in France on quasicrystals (crystals declared non-existent by orthodoxies of 20th century science).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.consulfrance-atlanta.org/spip.php?article4002|title=Claire Berger, graphene alchemist|work=France in the Southeast region|accessdate=28 December 2014}}</ref> 

== Career ==
Having studied and produced amorphous films in a postdoctoral position at the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]] (CEA), in 1988 she joined the [[Institut Néel]] in Grenoble, where she worked on electronic properties of [[Quasi-crystals (supramolecular)|quasi-crystals]].<ref name=":1" /> She was hired as a researcher at the CNRS's Laboratory for Study of Electronic Properties of Solids (LEPES), where she contributed to the experimental evidence for a metal-insulator transition in the compound quasicrystalline materials grown and characterised at LEPES.

Berger moved to Georgia Tech in 2001.<ref name=":0" />

She is notable for her co-authorship of the first article demonstrating the two dimensional properties of [[graphene]] and for proposing the use of graphene in electronics. Together with [[Walt de Heer]] and [[Phil First]] she co-authored the first patent for graphene electronics in 2003.<ref name="Physics" />

Her current scientific interests are primarily in the field of nano science and the electronic properties of graphene-based systems.<ref name="Physics" />

== Selected publications ==

* ''Exceptional ballistic transport in epitaxial graphene nanoribbons'', with J. Baringhaus, M. Ruan , F. Edler, A. Tejeda, M. Sicot, A. Taleb-Ibrahimi, A.P. Li, Z. Jiang, E.H. Conrad, C. Tegenkamp, W. A. de Heer, in ''Nature'' No.&nbsp;506, 2014, {{p.|349}}.
* ''Crystalline Silicon Transfer: A'' Top-Down ''Solution to Integrate Epitaxial Graphene into Silicon CMOS'', with R. Dong, Z. Guo, M. Ruan, J. Kunc, S. K Bhattacharya, W. A. de Heer, in ''J. Phys D'', 47, 094001, 8pp, 2014.
* ''A wide band gap metal-semiconductor-metal nanostructure made entirely from graphene'', with J. Hicks, A. Tejeda, A. A. Taleb-Ibrahimi, M.S. Nevius, F. F. Wang, K. Shepperd, J. J. Palmer, F. Bertran, P. Le Fèvre, J. Kunc, W. A. de Heer, E.H. Conrad, in ''Nature Physics'' No.&nbsp;9, 2013, {{p.|49}}.
* ''Record Maximum Oscillation Frequency in C-face Epitaxial Graphene transistors'', with Z. Guo, R. Dong, P.S. Chakraborty, N. Lourenco, J. Palmer, Y. Hu, M. Ruan, J. Hankinson, J. Kunc, J. D. Cressler, W. A. de Heer, in ''Nano Letters'' No.&nbsp;13, 2013, {{p.|942}}.
* ''Epitaxial graphene on silicon carbide: Introduction to structured graphene'', with M. Ruan, Y. Hu, Z. Guo, R. Dong, J. Palmer, J. Hankinson, W. A. de Heer, in ''MRS Bulletin'' No.&nbsp;37, 2012, {{p.|1146}}.
